tasks.prompt: Order the return to service sequence for a disinfected well.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional municipal well in western Canada disinfected after pump replacement, following provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: well disinfected and held through clearance sampling and connection to the system.

cards.label: Pump the well to waste until the heavy chlorine from disinfection is flushed out
Continue pumping until the chlorine residual falls to near the normal system level
Collect a bacteriological sample from the well sample tap
Receive an absent bacteriological result from the laboratory
Place the well into service at a controlled rate
Monitor residual and turbidity as the well comes fully online

tasks.explanation: A disinfected well is pumped to waste until the strong chlorine is gone, and it is only connected after an absent bacteriological result confirms the disinfection worked.

tasks.prompt: Order the bacteriological sampling and chain of custody sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional routine distribution bacteriological sample in western Canada, collected in a sterile bottle with sodium thiosulfate.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the sterile bottle through delivery to the laboratory.

cards.label: Wash hands and confirm the sterile bottle seal is intact and within its expiry
Disinfect the sample tap and flush it to draw fresh main water
Reduce the flow and fill the bottle without touching the rim or rinsing out the preservative
Cap the bottle immediately and label it with location, date, and time
Complete the chain of custody form and place the sample in a cooler with ice packs
Deliver the sample to the laboratory within the allowed holding time

tasks.explanation: Bacteriological sampling protects sterility at every step: the tap is disinfected, the bottle is never rinsed or touched at the rim, and the chilled sample reaches the lab inside its holding time with custody paperwork.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a grab turbidity measurement on filtered water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional bench turbidimeter check of filter effluent at a small plant in western Canada.
tasks.configuration: Scope: drawing the sample through recording the verified result.

cards.label: Draw the sample from the filter effluent tap after a brief flush
Fill a clean sample vial and wipe the outside dry and free of fingerprints
Insert the vial into the calibrated turbidimeter with the index mark aligned
Read and record the turbidity result
Compare the result with the continuous analyzer reading
Investigate and note any difference beyond the plant tolerance

tasks.explanation: A grab turbidity result is only trustworthy with a clean, bubble free vial in a calibrated meter, and comparing it with the continuous analyzer verifies the online instrument.

tasks.prompt: Order the bench pH measurement procedure for a treated water sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada measuring pH on a bench meter calibrated at the start of the shift.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the meter through recording the sample result.

cards.label: Rinse the pH electrode with deionized water and blot it dry without wiping
Calibrate the meter with fresh buffer solutions in the order given by the plant procedure
Rinse the electrode again and place it in the well mixed sample
Allow the reading to stabilize fully before noting the value
Record the pH, sample temperature, location, and time
Rinse the electrode and return it to its storage solution

tasks.explanation: Accurate pH depends on a clean, freshly calibrated electrode and a fully stabilized reading, and the electrode is protected by returning it to storage solution after use.

tasks.prompt: Order the alkalinity titration procedure for a raw water sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional bench alkalinity test in western Canada used to guide coagulant dosing for the day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing the sample and reagents through calculating the alkalinity result.

cards.label: Measure the set sample volume into a clean flask and record the volume
Add the indicator solution specified in the plant bench procedure
Fill the burette with the standard acid titrant and record the starting reading
Titrate slowly with constant swirling until the indicator reaches its endpoint colour
Record the final burette reading and calculate the acid volume used
Calculate the alkalinity from the acid volume and sample volume and record the result

tasks.explanation: A titration is only as good as its measured sample, careful endpoint, and recorded burette difference, so each step is completed and noted before the calculation is made.

tasks.prompt: Order the DPD free chlorine measurement procedure in the plant laboratory.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada checking free chlorine on a clearwell sample with a bench colorimeter.
tasks.configuration: Scope: drawing the sample through recording the verified result.

cards.label: Draw a fresh sample and begin the test immediately to avoid chlorine loss
Rinse the sample cell with the sample and fill it to the mark
Zero the colorimeter with the untreated sample cell
Add the DPD reagent for free chlorine to a second cell of sample and mix
Read the result within the method time limit and record it
Compare the result with the online analyzer and note any difference beyond tolerance

tasks.explanation: Free chlorine fades quickly, so the sample is tested at once, the meter is zeroed on untreated sample, and the reagent reading is taken inside the method time and checked against the analyzer.

tasks.prompt: Order the raw water sampling routine at a river intake.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional weekly raw water sample collection at a river intake in western Canada during spring conditions.
tasks.configuration: Scope: preparing bottles at the plant through samples packed for transport.

cards.label: Prepare labelled bottles and preservatives for each parameter on the sampling plan
Travel to the intake and note river conditions, weather, and any unusual appearance or odour
Collect the samples at the designated intake point without disturbing bottom sediment
Preserve and cap each sample as its method requires immediately after collection
Record field measurements for temperature, pH, and turbidity at the intake
Pack the samples chilled with the completed custody forms for delivery to the laboratory

tasks.explanation: Raw water sampling records the source conditions alongside the bottles, collects without disturbing sediment, preserves each sample at once, and packs everything chilled with custody forms.

tasks.prompt: Order the treated water compliance sampling day routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada completing a scheduled sampling day under provincial drinking water requirements and the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: reviewing the sampling plan through all samples delivered.

cards.label: Review the sampling plan and confirm locations, parameters, and bottle types for the day
Collect the plant treated water samples first, before leaving the plant
Collect distribution samples in the planned route order, flushing each tap as required
Label every bottle at the time of collection with location, date, and time
Complete the custody forms and check them against the bottles collected
Deliver all samples to the laboratory within their holding times and file the sampling record

tasks.explanation: A compliance sampling day is planned before it is collected, plant samples come first, every bottle is labelled at collection, and custody forms are checked against bottles before delivery.

tasks.prompt: Order the cold weather sample transport procedure for a northern western Canadian system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in a northern community in western Canada shipping winter samples to a distant laboratory.
tasks.configuration: Scope: samples collected through samples received by the laboratory in good condition.

cards.label: Collect the samples and complete labels and custody forms indoors where they stay dry
Place the bottles in a cooler with ice packs separated so bottles cannot freeze against them
Add insulation and a temperature indicator as the plant winter procedure requires
Keep the cooler inside the heated vehicle cab during transport, never in an unheated cargo area
Deliver the cooler to the carrier or laboratory the same day and note the time
Confirm receipt with the laboratory and file the transport record

tasks.explanation: Winter transport protects samples from both warming and freezing: bottles are insulated from direct ice pack contact, ride in the heated cab, and are delivered and confirmed the same day.

tasks.prompt: Order the quality control sampling sequence for a duplicate and a blank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada collecting scheduled quality control samples alongside a routine distribution sample.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planning the quality control samples through submitting all three bottles.

cards.label: Collect the routine sample first using the normal sterile technique
Collect the duplicate sample immediately after, at the same tap and in the same way
Prepare the blank by filling a sterile bottle with the laboratory supplied blank water
Label the duplicate and blank so the laboratory cannot tell them from routine samples
List all three samples on the custody form in collection order
Submit the full set together, chilled and within the holding time

tasks.explanation: A duplicate must be a true second collection at the same tap right after the first, and a blind blank tests the whole handling path, so both travel with the routine sample as one set.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator response sequence after receiving an adverse bacteriological result.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional municipal system in western Canada that receives an adverse bacteriological result from its laboratory, following provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: receipt of the adverse result through the required notifications and resampling.

cards.label: Receive and confirm the adverse result and the sample details from the laboratory
Notify the provincial regulator contact and the local health authority as soon as possible as provincial requirements direct
Notify the system owner and the operator in charge
Carry out any public notice or advisory directed by the health authority
Take corrective action such as flushing and raising the disinfectant residual in the affected area
Collect resamples at the required locations and confirm the follow up results before standing down the response

tasks.explanation: An adverse result puts notification first alongside corrective action, and the response is not closed until resampling confirms the water is back to standard.

tasks.prompt: Order the receiving and storage checks for a bulk chemical delivery.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional delivery of bulk sodium hypochlorite to a treatment plant in western Canada.
tasks.configuration: Scope: tanker arriving at the plant gate through the chemical placed in storage.

cards.label: Verify the delivery paperwork matches the product and quantity ordered
Inspect the tanker connections and the plant fill line before transfer
Confirm the receiving tank has enough free volume for the delivery
Connect the transfer line and open valves in the correct order with spill containment in place
Monitor the transfer and tank level until the delivery is complete
Disconnect, close and tag the fill line, and record the delivery in the chemical log

tasks.explanation: A safe chemical transfer starts with paperwork, connections, and confirmed tank capacity, keeps containment in place during transfer, and ends with the fill point secured and the delivery logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a liquid alum feed system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional alum metering pump system in western Canada being started at the beginning of a production run.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alum storage tank through a verified feed rate at the rapid mix.

cards.label: Confirm the alum tank level and that the suction line is flooded
Open the suction and discharge valves on the feed line
Prime the metering pump until alum flows without air
Start the pump at the calculated stroke and speed setting for the target dose
Confirm flow with a calibration column drawdown check
Verify the dose by jar test or settled water turbidity and trim the setting

tasks.explanation: A metering pump is primed on a flooded suction with valves lined up first, then set to the calculated dose and proven by a calibration drawdown before the dose is trusted.

tasks.prompt: Order the dry polymer make down and feed start up sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada preparing a batch of dry polymer solution for use as a filter aid.
tasks.configuration: Scope: empty make down tank through aged solution feeding the process.

cards.label: Fill the make down tank with the set volume of clean water and start the mixer
Add the weighed dry polymer slowly into the mixing vortex so no clumps form
Mix for the full wetting time given in the plant procedure
Stop the mixer and allow the solution to age for the required hydration period
Transfer the aged solution to the feed tank and line up the feed pump
Start the feed at the calculated rate and confirm delivery by drawdown

tasks.explanation: Dry polymer must be wetted slowly into a vortex, mixed, and fully aged before feeding, because clumps and unhydrated polymer will not perform in the process.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a lime feed system for pH and alkalinity adjustment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional lime slurry feed system in western Canada being started after a weekend shutdown.
tasks.configuration: Scope: slurry tank check through a confirmed pH response in the treated water.

cards.label: Check the slurry tank level and start the tank mixer to resuspend settled lime
Flush the feed line with water and confirm it is clear before starting the slurry pump
Start the slurry feed pump at the calculated setting for the target dose
Confirm slurry is reaching the application point and no line is plugging
Measure treated water pH after the mixing and reaction time has passed
Trim the feed to hold the target pH and record the dose and results in the log

tasks.explanation: Lime slurry settles and plugs lines, so the tank is mixed and the line is proven clear with water first, and the dose is judged by the pH measured after reaction time.

tasks.prompt: Order the powdered activated carbon feed sequence for a taste and odour event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada starting powdered activated carbon feed during an algae related taste and odour event on its reservoir source.
tasks.configuration: Scope: decision to feed carbon through confirmed taste and odour improvement.

cards.label: Confirm the event with raw water observations and any customer complaint pattern
Check carbon stock, slurry tank, and feed line condition before starting
Make down a carbon slurry batch at the plant procedure strength and start its mixer
Start the carbon feed at the rapid mix at the calculated starting dose
Monitor settled and filtered water for carbon carryover and adjust the dose as needed
Confirm improvement by treated water taste and odour checks and record the event and doses

tasks.explanation: Carbon feed is started only on a confirmed event, is applied at the rapid mix for maximum contact, and is watched for carryover while treated water checks prove it is working.

tasks.prompt: Order the response sequence for a small chemical spill inside the plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional small sodium hypochlorite spill in western Canada contained within the chemical room bund during a tank filling.
tasks.configuration: Scope: spill first noticed through the area returned to normal use.

cards.label: Stop the transfer or feed causing the spill and leave the area if fumes are strong
Put on the protective equipment listed for the product on its safety data sheet
Contain the spill within the bund using the spill kit pads and socks
Collect the absorbed material into the labelled waste container provided for it
Wash the contained area as the plant procedure directs and inspect for damage
Report the spill, record it in the log, and restock the spill kit items used

tasks.explanation: A small spill response stops the source first, protects the operator, contains before cleaning, and ends with reporting and a restocked spill kit.

tasks.prompt: Order the day tank filling sequence from the bulk hypochlorite tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada filling the hypochlorite day tank from the bulk storage tank.
tasks.configuration: Scope: day tank running low through the day tank filled and the feed uninterrupted.

cards.label: Confirm the day tank level and calculate the volume needed to fill it
Confirm the bulk tank has enough product and that the transfer line valves are correctly lined up
Put on the required protective equipment and place containment under the connections
Start the transfer pump and monitor both tank levels during the fill
Stop the transfer at the target day tank level and close the valves in order
Record the volumes transferred and both tank levels in the chemical log

tasks.explanation: Day tank filling is calculated before it is started, monitored at both tanks while it runs, and recorded from measured levels when it finishes.

tasks.prompt: Order the metering pump calibration column check procedure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada verifying the delivered rate of a coagulant metering pump.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pump running at its normal setting through the verified rate recorded.

cards.label: Fill the calibration column from the pump suction supply and note the starting level
Line up the valves so the pump draws from the column instead of the tank
Run the pump at its normal setting for the timed test period
Read the volume drawn from the column during the test period
Calculate the delivered rate and compare it with the target feed rate
Return the valves to the tank supply, adjust the pump if needed, and record the check

tasks.explanation: A calibration check isolates the pump onto a measured column, times a drawdown at the normal setting, and only then compares the delivered rate with the target.

tasks.prompt: Order the weekly chemical storage housekeeping inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 1 operator in western Canada completing the weekly chemical area inspection.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entering the chemical storage area through the completed inspection record.

cards.label: Check that incompatible chemicals are stored apart and all containers are labelled
Inspect tanks, drums, and piping for leaks, corrosion, and damaged fittings
Confirm containment areas are empty of rainwater and spilled product and drains are closed
Check tank levels against the inventory record and note any unexplained difference
Confirm the eyewash, safety shower, and spill kit are accessible and in date
Record the inspection, correct minor issues at once, and report defects to the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: The weekly inspection checks separation and labels, containment and leaks, true inventory, and life safety equipment, in that order, and records defects the same day.

tasks.prompt: Order the procedure to prepare a batch of diluted chemical solution.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada preparing a diluted polymer solution batch in a mix tank following the plant procedure.
tasks.configuration: Scope: empty mix tank through the finished batch ready for the feed pump.

cards.label: Calculate the chemical and water quantities needed for the target batch strength and volume
Put on the protective equipment required for the concentrated product
Add the measured water volume to the mix tank first
Add the measured chemical slowly to the water with the mixer running
Mix for the full time given in the procedure and confirm the solution looks uniform
Label the tank with product, strength, date, and preparer and record the batch in the chemical log

tasks.explanation: A safe batch is calculated first, water goes in before chemical, mixing is timed and confirmed, and the finished batch is labelled so no one has to guess its strength.

tasks.prompt: Order the start up of a centrifugal treated water pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional high lift centrifugal pump in western Canada being placed into service after a weekend shutdown.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pump at rest through the pump running at its duty point.

cards.label: Inspect the pump and motor and confirm the area is clear and dry
Confirm the pump casing is primed and the suction valve is fully open
Check that the discharge valve is closed or at its start position
Start the motor and watch pressure and current as the pump comes up to speed
Open the discharge valve slowly until the duty flow is reached
Record flow, pressures, and any unusual noise or vibration

tasks.explanation: A centrifugal pump starts primed with suction open and discharge throttled, then the discharge is opened slowly to the duty point while pressures and current confirm a healthy start.

tasks.prompt: Order the planned shutdown of a centrifugal treated water pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional planned shutdown of one high lift pump in western Canada for seal inspection.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pump running at duty through the pump secured at rest.

cards.label: Confirm another pump or storage can carry the demand while this pump is out
Close the discharge valve slowly to unload the pump
Stop the motor once flow has fallen to near zero
Close the suction valve to isolate the pump
Drain or vent the casing if the pump will be opened
Apply lockout and tagout and record the shutdown in the log

tasks.explanation: A planned shutdown unloads the pump by throttling the discharge before stopping the motor, then isolates, drains, and locks out the machine in that order.

tasks.prompt: Order the duty and standby pump changeover sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional treated water pumping station in western Canada rotating duty between two identical pumps.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duty pump running through the standby pump carrying the full duty.

cards.label: Confirm the standby pump is primed, its valves are lined up, and its controls are in automatic
Start the standby pump and bring it up to pressure with its discharge throttled
Open the standby pump discharge slowly while closing the duty pump discharge
Stop the former duty pump once the new pump carries the full flow
Set the former duty pump as the standby and confirm its controls are ready
Record the changeover, run hours for both pumps, and the reason for the rotation

tasks.explanation: A changeover proves the standby pump under pressure before load is transferred, swaps discharge valves in a controlled overlap, and leaves the old duty pump ready as the new standby.

tasks.prompt: Order the standby generator load test sequence for the plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional diesel standby generator in western Canada due for its monthly load test.
tasks.configuration: Scope: generator in standby through the plant back on normal power.

cards.label: Notify plant staff and confirm the plant can tolerate the brief transfer interruptions
Inspect the generator fuel, oil, coolant, and battery condition before starting
Start the generator and allow it to warm up without load
Transfer plant load to the generator using the transfer switch procedure
Run under load for the set test period while recording voltage, frequency, and temperatures
Transfer load back to normal power, allow a cool down run, and return the generator to standby

tasks.explanation: A load test inspects fluids and battery first, warms the machine unloaded, proves it under real plant load with readings recorded, and returns it cooled down and ready in standby.

tasks.prompt: Order the valve exercise routine for plant process valves.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada completing the scheduled exercise of key plant valves.
tasks.configuration: Scope: first valve on the list through the completed exercise record.

cards.label: Review the valve list and notify operations which valves will be moved and when
Operate each valve slowly through its full travel from open to closed and back
Note any valve that is stiff, leaking at the stem, or short of full travel
Return each valve to its normal operating position and confirm the position indicator agrees
Lubricate stems and gearboxes where the plant procedure requires it
Record each valve exercised, its condition, and any follow up work needed

tasks.explanation: Valve exercising moves each valve slowly through full travel one at a time, returns it to its proven normal position, and records condition so a seized valve is found on a routine day, not during an emergency.

tasks.prompt: Order the flow meter verification check against a measured volume.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada checking a treated water flow meter against a clearwell level change.
tasks.configuration: Scope: steady pumping conditions through the verified meter error recorded.

cards.label: Establish steady flow with one pump running and no other inflow or outflow changes
Record the clearwell starting level and the flow meter totalizer reading at the same moment
Run for the set test period and record the flow rate shown by the meter
Record the clearwell ending level and totalizer reading at the same moment
Calculate the true volume from the level change and tank dimensions and compare it with the totalizer volume
Record the meter difference found and report it if it exceeds the plant tolerance

tasks.explanation: A volume check holds conditions steady, reads level and totalizer at the same moments, and compares the true tank volume change with what the meter counted.

tasks.prompt: Order the clearwell level instrument check against a manual measurement.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada verifying the clearwell level transmitter during a routine round.
tasks.configuration: Scope: transmitter reading normally through the comparison recorded.

cards.label: Note the level shown by the transmitter on the plant display
Measure the true water level manually with the gauge or tape at the access hatch
Convert the manual measurement to the same units and reference point as the display
Compare the two values and calculate the difference
Check the transmitter sensing line or sensor face for fouling if the difference is large
Record both values and the difference and report any fault beyond the plant tolerance

tasks.explanation: An instrument check trusts neither reading alone: the display value and a careful manual measurement are brought to the same reference and compared, and fouling is checked before a fault is declared.

tasks.prompt: Order the pump and motor lubrication check routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional monthly lubrication round in western Canada covering plant pumps and mixer drives.
tasks.configuration: Scope: first machine on the round through the completed lubrication record.

cards.label: Review the lubrication schedule and gather the specified lubricant for each machine
Check each bearing housing oil level or grease condition with the machine in its safe state
Add only the specified lubricant and only to the marked fill level
Wipe fittings and housings clean and check for leaks or overheating discolouration
Run or observe each machine briefly and listen for bearing noise after servicing
Record each machine serviced, the lubricant used, and any defect found

tasks.explanation: Lubrication uses the specified product only, fills to the mark and no further, and pairs every service with a look and listen check so a failing bearing is caught early.

tasks.prompt: Order the lockout and tagout sequence to prepare a mixer drive for maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional flocculation paddle drive in western Canada being prepared for gearbox maintenance by a mechanic.
tasks.configuration: Scope: drive running normally through the drive proven safe to work on.

cards.label: Notify operations and confirm the basin can be out of service for the work period
Stop the drive using the normal stop control
Open and lock the electrical disconnect and the local isolator for the drive
Apply personal locks and tags for each worker who will work on the drive
Try the start control to prove the drive cannot start, then return it to off
Release any stored mechanical energy and confirm the paddles cannot move before work begins

tasks.explanation: Lockout stops the machine, isolates and locks every energy source, proves the isolation with a try start, and releases stored energy before any hands go on the equipment.

tasks.prompt: Order the end of day equipment securing routine for an unattended overnight plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional small plant in western Canada that runs unattended overnight with alarm callout coverage.
tasks.configuration: Scope: last production checks through the plant secured for the night.

cards.label: Confirm clearwell and storage levels are high enough for overnight demand
Confirm chemical day tank levels will last until the morning round
Set duty and standby pumps and feeds to automatic and confirm alarms are enabled
Test the callout alarm with a simulated signal and confirm the on call operator receives it
Secure chemical areas, lock doors, and set building heat for the night
Record the securing checks and the on call contact in the daily log

tasks.explanation: Overnight securing proves water, chemicals, automatic controls, and the callout path in that order, because an unattended plant must survive and summon help without anyone present.

tasks.prompt: Order the winterizing sequence for outdoor sample lines and small piping.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada preparing exposed sample lines and small piping before the first hard freeze.
tasks.configuration: Scope: lines in normal service through lines protected for winter.

cards.label: List every exposed line and drain point that needs winter protection
Drain and blow out lines that will not be used during winter
Insulate lines that must stay in service and confirm the insulation is complete and dry
Test heat tracing on in service lines and confirm thermostats and alarms work
Open cabinet and enclosure heaters and confirm they run
Record each line winterized and any protection still outstanding in the maintenance log

tasks.explanation: Winterizing works from a complete list, drains what can be drained, and proves insulation, heat trace, and heaters on what must stay live, before the cold arrives.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator response when frazil ice begins to restrict a river intake.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional river intake in western Canada losing capacity on a very cold night as frazil ice builds on the screens.
tasks.configuration: Scope: first sign of falling intake level through intake capacity restored.

cards.label: Confirm the restriction by checking wet well level trend and screen differential
Reduce plant flow to match the intake capacity still available
Switch to the standby intake path or screen bay if the plant has one
Apply the plant ice control method for the screens, such as backflushing or air bubbling, as fitted
Monitor wet well level closely and draw on treated storage if the restriction continues
Record the event, outside temperature, and actions taken and notify the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: Frazil ice response matches plant demand to what the intake can still deliver, uses the standby path and the fitted ice control, and protects the community from treated storage while the event lasts.

tasks.prompt: Order the cold morning chemical feed check routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada checking chemical feeds on the coldest morning of the year so far.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entering the chemical area through all feeds proven for the day.

cards.label: Check chemical room temperature and confirm heaters and heat tracing are running
Inspect feed lines, pump heads, and fittings for freeze damage or leaks
Check bulk and day tank levels and look for thickened or crystallized product
Run each feed pump briefly and confirm flow by calibration column drawdown
Confirm injection points are clear and chemical is reaching the process
Record the checks and any cold related defect in the daily log

tasks.explanation: Cold affects chemistry and hardware together, so the room, the lines, the product condition, and a proven drawdown for every pump are all checked before the day relies on them.

tasks.prompt: Order the plant start up sequence after a winter power outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada restarting after a six hour winter power outage, with power now restored.
tasks.configuration: Scope: power restored through the plant back in normal production.

cards.label: Inspect the whole plant for freeze damage, burst lines, and water on floors before starting anything
Confirm building heat is restored and chemical lines are thawed and intact
Restart chemical feeds and confirm each one delivers by drawdown
Restart raw water and process equipment in the normal start up order at a low rate
Check treated water residual and turbidity and run to waste until both are on target
Raise flow to normal, complete the outage record, and notify the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: A winter outage restart inspects for freeze damage before any start, proves heat and chemical feed, and holds water to waste until quality is proven, because cold damage and poor quality are both likely after an outage.

tasks.prompt: Order the safe thawing sequence for a frozen plant water line.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada dealing with a frozen treated water line inside the plant pipe gallery.
tasks.configuration: Scope: frozen line discovered through the line back in normal service.

cards.label: Confirm the line is frozen and close its isolation valves on both sides
Open a downstream tap or drain to give expanding ice and water a relief path
Apply gentle heat along the line starting from the open end, using approved heating methods only
Watch for flow at the open tap and for leaks as the ice plug releases
Close the tap, repressurize the line slowly, and inspect every joint for freeze damage
Record the event and add insulation or heat trace repairs to the maintenance list

tasks.explanation: Safe thawing isolates the line, gives expansion a relief path, warms gently from the open end, and repressurizes slowly with a leak inspection, because a thawed line often reveals split fittings.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter bulk chemical delivery receiving sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional bulk hypochlorite delivery in western Canada arriving during a snowstorm with a frozen yard.
tasks.configuration: Scope: tanker booked in through the delivery completed and the yard safe.

cards.label: Clear and sand the delivery route and fill point area before the tanker arrives
Confirm the fill line and connections are thawed and free of ice
Verify the paperwork and receiving tank free volume as in the normal receiving procedure
Connect the transfer line with containment in place and keep the operator present throughout
Monitor the transfer closely for leaks at cold stiffened hoses and fittings
Disconnect, drain the line so no product freezes inside it, secure the fill point, and record the delivery

tasks.explanation: A winter delivery adds yard safety and thawed connections before the normal receiving checks, watches cold stiffened hoses during transfer, and drains the line afterward so product cannot freeze inside it.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter distribution sampling routine for an outdoor sample station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada collecting scheduled samples from an outdoor sample station in mid winter.
tasks.configuration: Scope: leaving the plant through samples secured for transport.

cards.label: Gather insulated sample carriers and confirm the station key and tools are in the vehicle
Clear snow from the station access and confirm the enclosure heater has kept the tap from freezing
Flush the tap as required and collect the samples without letting filled bottles sit in the cold
Place filled bottles directly into the insulated carrier inside the heated vehicle
Complete labels and custody forms inside the vehicle where paper stays dry
Return samples to the plant cooler or ship them the same day using the winter transport procedure

tasks.explanation: Winter sampling keeps the sampler, the tap, and the filled bottles warm in that order, and paperwork is done in the vehicle so cold and snow never compromise the samples.

tasks.prompt: Order the fall preparation sequence for plant heating and building systems.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada preparing its building and heating systems in autumn before winter.
tasks.configuration: Scope: heating systems idle since spring through all systems proven for winter.

cards.label: Service the main building heater and confirm it starts and runs through a full cycle
Test backup and portable heaters and confirm fuel supplies for each
Check and replace weatherstripping and door seals on exterior doors
Test heat tracing circuits and pipe insulation in unheated areas
Confirm freeze alarms report to the callout system with a test signal
Record every system tested and any repair still needed before winter in the maintenance log

tasks.explanation: Fall preparation proves heat in layers, main heater, backups, building seals, heat trace, and freeze alarms, while there is still time to repair what fails.

tasks.prompt: Order the spring thaw preparation sequence for a plant on a river source.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada preparing in late winter for spring thaw and runoff on its river source.
tasks.configuration: Scope: winter operation through the plant ready for high turbidity runoff water.

cards.label: Review last year runoff records for peak turbidity, duration, and doses used
Confirm coagulant and aid inventories are stocked for a sustained high dose period
Service and test raw and treated turbidity instruments before runoff begins
Check sludge handling capacity and clear accumulated sludge from the clarifier
Confirm jar test supplies are ready and the bench procedure is posted
Brief all operators on the runoff response plan and record the preparations in the log

tasks.explanation: Thaw preparation learns from last year records, stocks chemistry, proves instruments, frees sludge capacity, and briefs the team, all before the river changes.

tasks.prompt: Order the response sequence when treated water demand spikes during a cold snap.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional community system in western Canada facing high demand during a cold snap as residents run taps to prevent household freezing.
tasks.configuration: Scope: demand rising above normal through demand and supply back in balance.

cards.label: Confirm the demand rise from distribution flow and falling storage levels
Raise plant production in steps and bring the standby filter and pump into service
Watch raw water and chemical inventories against the higher production rate
Monitor distribution pressure and storage levels at a shorter interval
Issue a public message asking residents to run only a pencil thin stream where needed, through the system owner channels
Record the event and return equipment to normal rotation once demand falls

tasks.explanation: A cold snap response proves the demand is real, adds production in steps with inventories checked, watches storage closely, and uses a public message to trim the demand itself.

tasks.prompt: Order the confined space entry preparation sequence for a clearwell inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional trained crew in western Canada preparing to enter a clearwell cell for inspection under the plant confined space procedure.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entry planned through the entrant ready to enter.

cards.label: Complete the entry permit and confirm the space is isolated, drained, and locked out
Ventilate the space with clean air and confirm ventilation will run during the entry
Test the atmosphere for oxygen and hazardous gases before entry and record the results
Set up the attendant, rescue equipment, and communications at the entry point
Brief the entrant and attendant on duties, hazards, and the rescue plan
Allow entry only after the permit is signed and all checks are complete, with continuous monitoring during the work

tasks.explanation: Confined space preparation isolates and ventilates first, tests before anyone enters, stations an attendant with rescue ready, and signs the permit only when every control is in place.

tasks.prompt: Order the morning safety check for a hypochlorite storage and feed room.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada opening the hypochlorite room at the start of a shift.
tasks.configuration: Scope: approaching the room door through the room cleared for normal work.

cards.label: Check for chemical odour and the room ventilation running before entering
Enter and inspect tanks, piping, and pump heads for leaks or salt buildup
Confirm containment is empty and the room drain is closed
Check the eyewash and safety shower are accessible and run them briefly as scheduled
Confirm protective equipment and the spill kit are in place and complete
Record the room check and report any leak or defect before starting feed work

tasks.explanation: The room is checked from the doorway first for odour and ventilation, then for leaks and containment, and life safety equipment is proven before any feed work begins inside.

tasks.prompt: Order the protective equipment sequence for handling a concentrated chemical.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada preparing to open a concentrated coagulant drum and connect it to a feed line.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator at the drum through the connection made and equipment removed safely.

cards.label: Read the product safety data sheet and confirm the protective equipment required
Inspect gloves, eye protection, and apron for damage before putting them on
Put on eye protection and face protection, then apron, then chemical resistant gloves
Open and connect the drum slowly, keeping the face away from the opening
Close the drum and wipe the connection area clean when the transfer is finished
Remove gloves last after washing them, wash hands and face, and store the equipment clean

tasks.explanation: Protective equipment goes on in an order that protects eyes and body before hands touch the product, and gloves come off last after washing so contaminated surfaces never reach skin.

tasks.prompt: Order the safety preparation sequence for work beside an open treatment basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada preparing to clean the weirs of an operating clarifier from its walkway.
tasks.configuration: Scope: work planned through the operator ready to start on the walkway.

cards.label: Inspect the walkway, handrails, and grating for damage, ice, or algae slip hazards
Confirm the life ring and reaching pole are in place at the basin
Notify another operator of the work location and the expected duration
Put on the required fall protection or flotation equipment where the plant procedure requires it
Set tools out so nothing can fall into the basin or trip the operator
Begin work facing the water with a clear path back to the exit at all times

tasks.explanation: Basin work safety checks the walking surface and rescue equipment first, tells another operator where the work is, and only then puts the worker on the walkway with a clear exit path.

tasks.prompt: Order the weekly eyewash and safety shower test sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada completing the weekly test of the chemical area eyewash and shower station.
tasks.configuration: Scope: arriving at the station through the test recorded.

cards.label: Confirm the path to the station is clear and the station is accessible
Activate the eyewash and confirm both streams run clear and at a gentle rate
Activate the safety shower and confirm full flow from the shower head
Run both until the water is clear and note any low flow, leaks, or damage
Close the valves, confirm the station drains and resets correctly
Record the test with date and initials and report any defect for repair

tasks.explanation: The weekly test proves access first, then flow quality at both the eyewash and the shower, and records defects the same day so the station works when it is needed.

tasks.prompt: Order the new chemical approval and setup sequence before first use at the plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada introducing a new treatment chemical product for the first time.
tasks.configuration: Scope: product proposed through the product in labelled storage with operators briefed.

cards.label: Obtain the safety data sheet and confirm the product is approved for drinking water use
Confirm storage compatibility and prepare the correct labelled storage location
Receive the delivery using the normal chemical receiving checks
Label all storage and feed containers with the workplace label required for the product
Set up or adjust the feed equipment and confirm it is compatible with the product
Brief all operators on hazards, protective equipment, and feed settings and file the safety data sheet

tasks.explanation: A new chemical is approved and understood before it arrives, stored and labelled correctly on arrival, and no operator feeds it until everyone has been briefed from its safety data sheet.

tasks.prompt: Order the safe manual handling sequence for moving a full chemical drum.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada moving a full chemical drum from the delivery area to storage using a drum handler.
tasks.configuration: Scope: drum on the delivery dock through the drum secured in storage.

cards.label: Inspect the drum for leaks or damage and confirm its label and contents
Put on the protective equipment required for the product
Secure the drum in the drum handler and confirm it is balanced before moving
Move the drum along the planned clear route at walking pace
Set the drum down in its storage position inside containment
Remove the handler, confirm the drum is stable and capped, and record the move

tasks.explanation: Drum handling inspects and protects first, secures the load in the handler before it moves, and ends with the drum stable, capped, and inside containment.

tasks.prompt: Order the ladder and platform inspection sequence before basin maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada inspecting portable ladders and fixed platforms before a day of basin maintenance.
tasks.configuration: Scope: equipment gathered through all access equipment passed or removed from service.

cards.label: Inspect ladder rails, rungs, and feet for damage, looseness, or contamination
Check platform decking, toe boards, and handrails for damage or corrosion
Confirm fixed access points are clear of ice, algae, and stored materials
Tag and remove from service any ladder or platform that fails inspection
Set the passed ladder at the work location at the correct angle on firm footing
Record the inspections and any equipment removed from service in the maintenance log

tasks.explanation: Access equipment is inspected before it is trusted, failed items are tagged out at once, and only passed equipment is set up for the work.

tasks.prompt: Order the end of shift safety lockup sequence for the treatment plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada closing the plant at the end of the last staffed shift of the day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: work areas in use through the plant locked and alarmed.

cards.label: Return tools, hoses, and chemicals to their storage locations and close all chemical containers
Confirm no maintenance work is in progress and all lockout devices are accounted for
Check that basin walkways and chemical areas are clear and gates are closed
Turn off non essential equipment and confirm required systems remain in automatic
Lock all exterior doors and chemical storage areas
Set the security and freeze alarms and record the lockup in the daily log

tasks.explanation: Lockup restores order first, chemicals closed and tools stored, accounts for lockout devices, and only then locks and alarms the building.

tasks.prompt: Order the gas detector bump test and calibration check sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada preparing a portable gas detector for use before a wet well visit.
tasks.configuration: Scope: detector in its charger through the detector cleared for field use.

cards.label: Inspect the detector, sensor openings, and battery charge before removal from the charger
Turn the detector on in clean air and confirm it zeroes correctly
Apply the bump test gas and confirm each sensor responds and alarms
Calibrate the detector if any sensor fails the bump test or calibration is due
Confirm the detector passes a second bump test after any calibration
Record the test results and take only a passing detector into the field

tasks.explanation: A gas detector is trusted only after a clean air zero and a bump test prove every sensor responds, and a failed sensor means calibration and a retest, not field use.

tasks.prompt: Order the daily log completion sequence at the end of a production day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Class 1 operator in western Canada closing out the records for a normal production day.
tasks.configuration: Scope: last process readings taken through the signed daily log filed.

cards.label: Collect the final flows, levels, residuals, and turbidity readings for the day
Total the treated volume and chemical used and calculate the average doses
Enter any abnormal events, alarms, and corrective actions with their times
Check every required entry is complete and correct any gaps while the day is fresh
Sign the log and file it in the plant record system
Flag any item needing follow up on the handover note for the next operator

tasks.explanation: The daily log is completed from final readings first, totals and doses second, and events with times third, and it is signed and filed the same day with follow ups flagged.

tasks.prompt: Order the monthly operating report preparation sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in charge in western Canada preparing the monthly summary required under provincial drinking water requirements in general terms.
tasks.configuration: Scope: month ended through the report submitted and filed.

cards.label: Gather the daily logs, laboratory results, and chemical records for the month
Check the records for missing days or results and resolve any gaps
Summarize flows, treated volumes, and key water quality results for the month
List any adverse results, incidents, and corrective actions with their dates
Complete the report in the format the provincial requirements direct and have it reviewed
Submit the report by its due date and file the submitted copy with the monthly records

tasks.explanation: A monthly report is built from complete daily records, gaps are resolved before summarizing, incidents are listed with dates, and the submitted copy is filed as proof.

tasks.prompt: Order the alarm callout response sequence for an unattended plant at night.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional on call operator in western Canada receiving a high priority plant alarm at night.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alarm received at home through the plant stable and the event recorded.

cards.label: Acknowledge the alarm and note its type, time, and the plant readings available remotely
Contact the plant or a second operator if the alarm suggests an immediate public safety risk
Travel to the plant safely and confirm the alarm condition on arrival
Take the corrective action in the plant response procedure for that alarm
Confirm the plant is stable and reset the alarm only after the condition is cleared
Record the callout, travel and arrival times, findings, and actions in the log

tasks.explanation: A callout starts with information, not speed: the alarm is understood from remote readings first, the condition is confirmed on site, and the alarm is reset only after the cause is cleared.

tasks.prompt: Order the wellhead protection routine inspection for a municipal well.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada completing the scheduled inspection of a municipal well and its wellhead protection area.
tasks.configuration: Scope: arriving at the well site through the inspection recorded.

cards.label: Check the well site fencing, gate, and signage and confirm the area is secure
Inspect the well cap, vent, and sanitary seal for damage or openings
Look for standing water, spills, or new potential contaminant sources near the wellhead
Check the well house, piping, and sample tap for leaks or damage
Record the static and pumping water levels if the inspection includes them
File the inspection record and report any deficiency to the operator in charge the same day

tasks.explanation: Wellhead inspection works from the protection area inward, security and land use first, then the cap and seal that keep contaminants out, and deficiencies are reported the same day.

tasks.prompt: Order the routine well pumping check sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in western Canada completing the weekly pumping check on a municipal supply well.
tasks.configuration: Scope: well running normally through the check results recorded.

cards.label: Record the pumping water level and the flow rate shown for the well
Record the pump run hours and calculate the volume pumped since the last check
Listen for abnormal pump noise and check for vibration or air in the discharge
Collect a raw water sample if the check schedule requires one
Compare levels, flow, and specific capacity trend with previous checks
Record the results and report any declining trend to the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: A well check records level and flow together, turns run hours into volume, and compares the trend with past checks so a declining well is spotted early.

tasks.prompt: Order the taste and odour complaint investigation sequence at the plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada receiving several taste and odour complaints from one area of the community.
tasks.configuration: Scope: complaints received through the cause found or ruled out and the response recorded.

cards.label: Log each complaint with location, time, and the description given
Check treated water chlorine residual and recent plant process changes
Collect residual and appearance samples in the complaint area after a tap flush
Check raw water for algae growth or runoff changes that could cause the odour
Flush the affected area or adjust treatment if the checks point to a cause
Record the investigation and inform the system owner contact of the findings and actions

tasks.explanation: A complaint investigation logs the pattern first, checks the plant and the local water in order, and only flushes or adjusts treatment when the checks point to a cause.

tasks.prompt: Order the response sequence for a low clearwell level alarm during production.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada where the clearwell level falls below its low alarm during a high demand morning.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alarm sounding through clearwell level recovered and stable.

cards.label: Confirm the level with the local gauge to rule out an instrument fault
Check distribution demand and confirm whether a pump or major use is driving the fall
Raise filtration rate and bring any standby filter into service
Reduce distribution pumping if the level continues to fall toward the minimum for contact time
Hold the minimum level that protects disinfection contact time at all costs
Record the event, the lowest level reached, and the actions taken and notify the operator in charge

tasks.explanation: A low clearwell response verifies the level, finds whether production or demand is at fault, adds production first, and protects the contact time minimum level above all else.

tasks.prompt: Order the power failure response sequence at the treatment plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional plant in western Canada losing normal power during a production day, with a standby generator fitted.
tasks.configuration: Scope: power failing through the plant running on standby power or safely shut down.

cards.label: Confirm the outage and check that the standby generator has started and taken load
If the generator has not started, shut down chemical feeds and secure the plant for a safe stop
Check treated storage levels and estimate how long supply can be maintained
Notify the operator in charge and the power utility and record the outage start time
Monitor generator fuel and plant conditions at a shorter interval while on standby power
When normal power returns, restart in the normal order, prove water quality, and complete the outage record

tasks.explanation: A power failure response proves standby power first, secures chemistry if there is none, plans around stored water, and restarts in the normal order with quality proven before supply resumes.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual plant maintenance planning sequence.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional operator in charge in western Canada building the annual maintenance plan for a small treatment plant.
tasks.configuration: Scope: last year records reviewed through the new plan scheduled and assigned.

cards.label: Review last year maintenance records, breakdowns, and outstanding defects
Inspect each major asset and update its condition in the asset record
List the preventive tasks due for each asset and the parts and supplies each one needs
Schedule the tasks through the year around demand and source water seasons
Assign each task to an operator or contractor and set its due date
Record the plan and review it monthly so overdue tasks are rescheduled, not lost

tasks.explanation: Annual planning starts from what actually failed and what is still outstanding, inspects before scheduling, and assigns every task an owner and a date so the plan can be followed up.

tasks.prompt: Settled-water turbidity climbed from 1.9 NTU to 4.8 NTU over two days at a prairie plant while the alum dose stayed at the setting used all month.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: Raw-water turbidity rose from 20 NTU to 58 NTU after spring runoff reached the reservoir.
The alum feed rate and pump setting were not changed during the two days.
Jar tests run today settle best at a dose about 40 percent higher than the current plant dose, leaving 1.5 NTU.
Floc in the basin is small and sparse, and much of it does not settle in a grab sample left standing 30 minutes.
Raw-water pH and alkalinity are in their usual range, and rapid mix and flocculator speeds are normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum dose is too high and the particles have restabilized
The alum dose is now too low for the higher raw-water solids load
The flocculators are shearing floc that formed correctly
The settled-water turbidimeter has drifted high

inference.explanation: Raw turbidity nearly tripled while the dose stayed fixed, floc is small and unsettled, and jar tests settle well at a higher dose. That fits an underdose. Restabilization needs an excessive dose, shear would break down floc that had formed, and a drifted meter would not match the unsettled grab sample.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms that the dose failed to track raw-water demand?

options.label: Archived filter backwash volume log
Archived jar test series and dose log from the last runoff event
Archived finished-water hardness log

nextClue.explanation: Archived jar test series and dose log from the last runoff event directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Backwash volumes were normal last month, which says nothing about coagulant demand in the basin.
clueText.nc-b: Last runoff, the jar test optimum rose with raw turbidity in the same way, and raising the plant dose restored settled turbidity below 2 NTU.
clueText.nc-c: Hardness records are steady and unrelated to floc formation or settling.

tasks.prompt: Two days after the alum dose was raised to handle turbid runoff, floc quality collapsed and settled turbidity rose sharply at a western Canadian plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: The alum dose was doubled two days ago and has stayed at the higher rate.
Raw-water alkalinity fell from 86 mg/L to 28 mg/L as CaCO3, and coagulation pH fell from 7.1 to 6.0.
The soda ash day bin is empty and the feeder shows a no-flow alarm that was acknowledged but not cleared.
Jar tests with added alkalinity form large, fast-settling floc at the current alum dose.
Raw-water turbidity is unchanged since the dose increase.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The higher alum dose restabilized the particles by charge reversal
Cold raw water slowed the flocculation reaction
Alum consumption of alkalinity, with no alkalinity replacement, dropped the pH out of the effective coagulation range
The flocculator paddles are turning too fast and shearing floc

inference.explanation: Alkalinity fell by two thirds and pH dropped a full unit after the dose doubled, the soda ash feeder is empty, and jar tests recover when alkalinity is added. That is an alkalinity and pH crash. The jar recovery with alkalinity, not a lower dose, rules against restabilization, and no temperature or paddle change is observed.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms the alkalinity feed failure?

options.label: Archived raw-water temperature log
Archived clarifier sludge blanket survey
Archived soda ash feeder run log and bin level record for the past week

nextClue.explanation: Archived soda ash feeder run log and bin level record for the past week directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Raw-water temperature held near 11 C all week, which does not explain an alkalinity loss of this size.
clueText.nc-b: The blanket survey was normal, which rules out a settling problem but does not track chemical feed.
clueText.nc-c: The feeder log shows no soda ash delivered for three days while alum feed doubled, and the bin record shows it empty since the first day.

tasks.prompt: In mid-January at a northern Alberta plant, floc is weak and slow forming and settled turbidity is 3.9 NTU, although the same dose worked well in October.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: Raw-water temperature is 1 C, down from 14 C in October.
Jar tests at the current dose eventually form good floc, but take roughly three times longer than in October.
The alum dose, rapid mix, and flocculator settings match the October settings that produced 1.4 NTU settled water.
Raw-water turbidity, pH, and alkalinity are similar to October values.
Extending flocculation time in the jar test restores settled turbidity to about 1.5 NTU.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum stock has lost strength over the winter
Raw-water alkalinity has been consumed by the alum dose
The sedimentation basin is short-circuiting
Cold water is slowing floc formation, so the available flocculation time is no longer enough

inference.explanation: Only temperature changed materially, jar floc forms well but slowly, and longer flocculation time restores performance. That fits cold water kinetics. Alkalinity is unchanged, the same chemical works given time, and a short circuit would not slow floc growth in a jar.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms a seasonal cold water pattern?

options.label: Archived winter operating records showing settled turbidity versus raw-water temperature for three past winters
Archived alum delivery certificates
Archived distribution pressure log

nextClue.explanation: Archived winter operating records showing settled turbidity versus raw-water temperature for three past winters directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Each past winter, settled turbidity rose as raw water fell below 4 C and recovered in spring at the same dose, matching this year.
clueText.nc-b: Alum certificates show the delivered product met specification, which does not explain a pattern tied to temperature.
clueText.nc-c: Distribution pressures were normal, which has no bearing on floc formation time in the plant.

tasks.prompt: Settled turbidity got worse after the operator raised the alum dose twice to chase rising raw-water colour, and the water now carries fine, dispersed solids.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: The alum dose is now about double the jar test dose that worked last week.
A jar test series today shows settled turbidity lowest at a mid-range dose, and higher at both lower and higher doses.
Coagulation pH has fallen from 7.0 to 6.2 as the dose increased.
Floc at the current dose is tiny and dispersed, and a settled sample stays cloudy for hours.
Raw-water colour and turbidity have been steady for two days.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum dose is excessive, restabilizing particles and depressing pH
The alum dose is still too low for the raw-water load
The flocculator is shearing large floc into fine floc
The clarifier sludge blanket has risen into the effluent launders

inference.explanation: The jar curve is U-shaped with its best point well below the current dose, pH fell as dose rose, and solids stay dispersed. That is overdose restabilization. A low dose contradicts the jar optimum being lower, shear needs large floc forming first, and no blanket observation supports the last option.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms the overdose pattern?

options.label: Archived sludge blanket depth survey
Archived jar test dose curve and plant dose trend for the past week
Archived flocculator motor current log

nextClue.explanation: Archived jar test dose curve and plant dose trend for the past week directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Blanket depth was mid-range and steady, which does not explain dispersed solids that will not settle in a jar.
clueText.nc-b: The archived curve shows settled turbidity rising steadily once the plant dose passed the jar optimum, exactly as it did this week.
clueText.nc-c: Flocculator current was normal, which argues against a mechanical mixing change.

tasks.prompt: Floc formation stopped almost completely over one shift even though the alum pump is running and stroking normally.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: The alum day tank level has not dropped at all during the shift.
Pressure at the pump discharge gauge is well above its normal reading.
No flow is visible at the injection point sample tap, and the feed line past the pump is cool and still.
A jar test dosed by hand from the day tank forms normal floc at the usual dose.
Raw-water turbidity, pH, and alkalinity are unchanged.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum in the day tank has lost its strength
The alum feed line or injection quill is plugged, so no coagulant is reaching the water
The alum pump has lost its prime and is pumping air
Raw-water demand rose beyond what the dose can treat

inference.explanation: The tank level is static, discharge pressure is high, and nothing arrives at the injection tap, while hand-dosed tank chemical works fine in a jar. That is a blockage downstream of the pump. Weak chemical is disproven by the jar test, a lost prime usually gives low rather than high discharge pressure, and raw demand is unchanged.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms a recurring injection point blockage?

options.label: Archived alum supplier strength certificates
Archived raw-water turbidity trend
Archived maintenance log for the injection quill and feed line

nextClue.explanation: Archived maintenance log for the injection quill and feed line directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Supplier certificates show the alum met strength specification, matching the good jar test result.
clueText.nc-b: Raw turbidity was flat all shift, which rules out a demand surge as the cause.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows the quill was last cleaned 14 months ago and has plugged twice before with the same high discharge pressure and zero tank drawdown.

tasks.prompt: Floc in the flocculation basin is patchy, with dense clouds of good floc beside stretches of milky, untreated-looking water, and settled turbidity is poor.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: The rapid mix motor current reads zero and the mixer shaft is not turning, although its run light is on.
Alum is being fed at the normal rate into the rapid mix chamber.
Jar tests mixed vigorously for one minute form uniform, good floc at the plant dose.
Basin samples taken across the chamber vary widely, from well flocculated to almost raw.
Raw-water quality and the flocculator paddles are normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum dose is too low for the raw water
The flocculator speed is too high and is shearing floc
The rapid mixer has failed, so coagulant is not being dispersed through the raw water
The raw water alkalinity is too low for coagulation

inference.explanation: The mixer is not turning, samples vary from treated to almost raw across the chamber, and vigorous hand mixing in a jar fixes the result at the same dose. That is failed dispersion. Dose, shear, and alkalinity do not explain untreated pockets beside good floc.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms when the rapid mixer stopped?

options.label: Archived motor current trend and run status history for the rapid mixer
Archived jar test results from last month
Archived settled-water turbidity summary

nextClue.explanation: Archived motor current trend and run status history for the rapid mixer directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Current dropped to zero at 03:10 and stayed there, and the patchy floc was first noted on the next round, matching the failure time.
clueText.nc-b: Last month the jar tests were normal, which only confirms the dose was right before the failure.
clueText.nc-c: The summary is monthly and cannot pinpoint a failure that began this shift.

tasks.prompt: One of two parallel flocculation and settling trains produces poor settled water while the other train, on the same raw water and dose, performs normally.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: Train 2 settled turbidity is 1.3 NTU and Train 1 settled turbidity is 4.1 NTU at the same flow.
Both trains receive the same coagulated water from a common rapid mix.
The Train 1 flocculator drive motor is running, but the paddle shaft in the basin does not rotate when watched through the hatch.
Floc leaving Train 1 is small and unformed, and floc leaving Train 2 is large and settles well.
A coupling guard on the Train 1 drive was found warm, with rubber dust beneath it.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: The alum dose is wrong for the raw water
Train 1 is hydraulically overloaded compared with Train 2
The Train 1 clarifier blanket has risen and is washing out
The Train 1 flocculator drive coupling has failed, so that train gets no gentle mixing

inference.explanation: Both trains share dose and raw water and carry the same flow, yet only Train 1 fails, its paddle shaft does not turn while the motor runs, and there is rubber dust at the coupling. That is a failed drive coupling. Dose and overload are common to both trains or equal, and no blanket observation is offered.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms the coupling failure point?

options.label: Archived flow split records for the two trains
Archived drive inspection and vibration notes for the Train 1 flocculator
Archived common rapid mix dose log

nextClue.explanation: Archived drive inspection and vibration notes for the Train 1 flocculator directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Flow split records show an even split all week, which removes overload from consideration.
clueText.nc-b: Notes from last month flagged rising vibration and coupling wear on Train 1 and recommended replacement, which was deferred.
clueText.nc-c: The dose log is steady and shared by both trains, so it cannot explain a one-train failure.

tasks.prompt: Sweep floc is poor and settled turbidity is high at a plant that doses lime with alum, and staff report a slippery feel at the plant tap.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: Coagulation pH reads 8.7, well above the plant target range of 6.8 to 7.4.
Raw-water alkalinity is normal, but treated alkalinity has risen to 160 mg/L as CaCO3.
The lime feeder is running continuously, including during a period when the control signal called for it to stop.
Jar tests at pH 7.1 form large sweep floc and settle to 1.2 NTU at the current alum dose.
Alum dose and raw-water turbidity have not changed.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Lime is being overfed, pushing pH above the range where alum forms good sweep floc
Alum is being underfed for the raw-water load
The raw water has turned cold and slowed flocculation
The rapid mixer has failed and coagulant is not dispersing

inference.explanation: pH is far above target, treated alkalinity climbed, the lime feeder runs when it should be stopped, and jars at normal pH settle well on the same alum dose. That is lime overfeed. Alum dose and temperature are unchanged, and dispersion problems would not raise alkalinity.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms the lime feeder control fault?

options.label: Archived raw-water temperature log
Archived alum day tank level record
Archived lime feeder output signal and run-time log

nextClue.explanation: Archived lime feeder output signal and run-time log directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: Raw temperature stayed near 12 C, which does not explain a pH of 8.7.
clueText.nc-b: Alum tank drawdown matches the set dose, which clears the alum feed.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows the feeder at full output for 26 hours, including 9 hours when the controller output was zero, confirming a stuck feeder control.

tasks.prompt: Settled and filtered turbidity are acceptable, but chlorine demand at the plant has jumped and coagulant demand is rising, with the raw water looking tea-coloured.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: A 0.45-micron filtered raw-water sample still measures 32 CU of colour, close to the unfiltered value of 35 CU.
Raw-water turbidity is low at 3 NTU and has not changed.
Jar tests need a higher alum dose than usual, and the extra dose mainly removes colour rather than turbidity.
The reservoir level is low after a dry prairie summer and the intake is drawing from a deeper, more organic-rich layer.
Dissolved organic carbon in the raw water measures 6.8 mg/L, up from a usual 3.5 mg/L.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by the observations?

options.label: Suspended solids from runoff are overloading the coagulation process
Dissolved organic matter in the source has increased, raising both coagulant and chlorine demand
The alum stock solution has been diluted
The colour meter is reading high because of turbidity interference

inference.explanation: Colour survives filtration, turbidity is low, dissolved organic carbon nearly doubled, and jars spend extra dose removing colour. That is dissolved organics, not suspended runoff. Diluted alum would not raise chlorine demand, and turbidity interference is contradicted by the low turbidity and the filtered reading.

nextClue.prompt: Which archived record best confirms the source organic shift?

options.label: Archived raw-water dissolved organic carbon and colour log by intake depth
Archived alum tank refill records
Archived turbidity meter calibration record

nextClue.explanation: Archived raw-water dissolved organic carbon and colour log by intake depth directly records the condition behind the keyed explanation over time, so it best confirms it against the alternatives.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows the deep intake layer has run near 7 mg/L dissolved organic carbon all month, roughly double the shallow layer used in spring.
clueText.nc-b: Refill records show alum delivered at normal strength, which clears the chemical stock.
clueText.nc-c: The turbidity meter calibrated within tolerance, and turbidity is low in any case.

tasks.prompt: Floc quality declined steadily over three days after the alum bulk tank was refilled, although pump settings and raw water are unchanged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian Class 1 water plant log: steady plant flow unless noted, archived plant and laboratory records available for review.

evidence.label: Jar tests dosed from a fresh sample bottle of alum form good floc at the normal dose.
Jar tests dosed from the plant day tank need nearly double the dose for the same result.
A density check of the day tank liquid reads well below the expected specific gravity for the alum product.
